pr_title: Skip path metadata lookup in bytestream uploader when artefact won't be uploaded
pr_body:
Fresh take on #23252 without the NPE.

This PR is an alternate implementation of #20575 that defers to `LocalFileType` where possible, adds a test case and fixes a latent NPE in `src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/runtime/NamedArtifactGroup.java` (path converter returns null for files lacking a digest, such as directories, symlinks and anything skipped under minimal mode).

This should improve performance. Benchmarking (in Bazel v6) has shown 54% of a Bazel profile for a fully cached build is spent in `readPathMetadata`. Gains likely won't be as significant as digest lookups are still required (required to produce bytestream URI).

Fixes #20576.

issue_context.title: perf: bazel computes digests for too many files when `remote_build_event_upload` is set to `minimal`
issue_context.body:
### Description of the bug:


when `--remote_build_event_upload` is set to `minimal`, bazel only uploads logs and profiles to the CAS. bazel does not appear to use this information to skip creating `PathMetadata` instances for files that aren't going to be uploaded to the CAS. as far as I can tell, the digests should only be computed for files that are going to be uploaded to the CAS.

I was able to make a fully cached remote build 3x (20min -> 7min) faster by skipping calling `digestUtil.compute(path)` for files that aren't going to be uploaded to the CAS ([example impl](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/20575)). as I mention in the PR description, I'm not entirely sure why this makes the overall build faster but the theory is that it allows the `bes-uploader` thread to process build events more quickly, reducing memory pressure.

comments: Since our monorepo isn't compatible with bazel 7 I've been testing based on 6.4.0. Results for this branch: https://github.com/christianscott/bazel/tree/christianscott-faster_cached_builds Memory usage before [`ackQueue` takes up ~40% of the heap](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/e7218d556a2a265183a10a19fcaa21c0277820ad/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/buildeventservice/BuildEventServiceUploader.java#L400) Memory usage after Forgot to take a heapdump

I intend to take a look at this in early 2024. In the vast majority of cases, the BES uploader shouldn't have to compute file digests; it should instead receive digests computed at an earlier stage (all action outputs have already been digested by the time an action is complete).
Thanks @tjgq. Please let me know if there's any more information or data I can share with you.

> it should instead receive digests computed at an earlier stage

btw @tjgq I may have misspoken, bazel may indeed be reusing the digests from a previous phase. I think the performance hit comes from the `stat` syscalls. I noticed that `stat` is run before the digest cache is checked. From memory the syscalls are cached per build, perhaps the `bes-uploader` doesn't share the syscall cache? I'll dig a bit deeper when I get some time

review_comments: I'm having a hard time trying to understand what functionally changes in this PR. What do we save by exiting early here, considering that we're still calling `digestUtil.compute`?

I find myself asking the same question. This went through a number of iterations, as I discovered more and more requirements that incrementally eliminated any kind of potential optimisation.

I'm going to close this. There is room for improvement in the bytestream uploader (I had a stab at some in #23252 but hit a NPE I could not track down, at face value the area seems like it would benefit from a refactor and perhaps alignment across full and minimal upload modes).

FWIW, I don't think the uploader should be digesting files at all; all output files have already been digested (and the digests cached in memory as a `FileArtifactValue`) during action execution, so we should figure out a way to plumb that data into the uploader.
Some spawn intermediate outputs might not be stored, though.
